title: A proof of Pythagoras with no words
statement: Take a right triangle with legs $a$ and $b$ and hypotenuse $c$. Using only four copies of it and one square, show that $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.
solutionSteps: Draw a square with side $a + b$. Its area is $(a + b)^2$.
Place the four triangles inside it, one along each edge, each with its right angle in a corner. The hole they leave in the middle is a square whose side is the hypotenuse, $c$.
Now add up the same area a second way: four triangles at $\tfrac{1}{2}ab$ each, plus the tilted square. That gives $4 \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}ab + c^2 = 2ab + c^2$.
Both expressions measure the same square, so $(a + b)^2 = 2ab + c^2$.
Expand the left side: $a^2 + 2ab + b^2 = 2ab + c^2$. Cancel the $2ab$ from both sides and you are left with $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.

figure.alt: A square of side a plus b containing four copies of the right triangle, arranged so the gap they leave in the middle is a tilted square whose side is the hypotenuse c.
